unresolvedReferences.description: Xiao Jingxian's court posts after Emperor Wu's accession (s0029-s0037) are undated, between 482 and Yongming 5 (487).
Xiao Jingxian's death at 50 is not explicitly dated; it followed the Yongming 5 (487) campaign.
Xiao Yi's execution with Wang Yan is not dated in the text; placed at the fall of Wang Yan (497).
Xiao Chifu's Liu Song-era posts (s0087-s0092) are undated.
Xiao Yingzhou's early career (s0111-s0116) is undated.
Xiao Yingzhou's posts under Emperor Wu (s0119-s0122) are undated.
Xiao Yingzhou's posts at Stone City, Guangling and Jingzhou (s0137-s0144) and the northern raid of s0140 are undated (between 495 and 500).
The officials Jiang, Xiao, Liu, Xu, Shen and Cao are named only by surname and office in the proclamation; not identified as separate people.
Zhang the Acting Governor of Xiang province and Wang of Si province are not identified by name.
Xiao Yaoxin's tenure in Jingzhou is dated only to the Jianwu era (494-498).
Xiao Yingzhou's death on renyin of the twelfth month of Zhongxing 1 may fall in early 502 in the Western calendar; recorded as 501.
The Prince of Yuzhang of Qi (Xiao Ni) is cited only as a ritual precedent and not extracted.
